subject: general
question: Under the British colonial rule, India's economy was basically agricultural. At that time, approximately how many percent of the country's population was directly or indirectly earning their livelihood from agriculture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**85.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Approximately **85% of the population in India** relied on **agriculture** for their livelihood during the **British colonial rule.**
 
• This was primarily because the British implemented policies that led to the **commercialization of agriculture **and the** displacement of traditional industries,** forcing people to depend on** agriculture for their survival.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The two main crops grown in pre-colonial India were **rice and wheat.**
 
• Despite this, it was** sustainable and self-sufficient.** 
 
• It is important to note that while agriculture played a crucial role in India's economy, it was also marked by widespread poverty, exploitation, and inequality under British rule.
